title: The Friday Hotfix
text: A fix has to ship tonight. A branch is merged and an artifact with the right name appears, ready to deploy.
held: It shipped tonight, and anyone could show where it came from.

cards.label: Refuse to build
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: branch
fields.check: Check which branch this came from

intrusion.detail: This commit is from a personal fork, not the release branch.
intrusion.why: Urgency is when the usual route gets skipped. A build from a fork is code nobody on the release branch approved.
intrusion.reveal: The hotfix commit came from a personal fork, not the protected branch.

temptations.label: Skip the tests: there's no time tonight
temptations.why: A hotfix that breaks checkout is a second incident. The checks are what make shipping at night survivable.

cards.label: Refuse to deploy
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: built
fields.ok: Built by the pipeline from the release branch.

intrusion.value: on a laptop, uploaded by hand
intrusion.detail: No pipeline provenance: this was built on a laptop and uploaded.
intrusion.why: The right name on an artifact built by hand is the classic route for a backdoor during an incident.
intrusion.reveal: The hotfix artifact had been built on a laptop and uploaded by hand.

teaches: Incidents are when controls get waived, which is why attackers like them.
The fast path and the safe path should be the same path.

question.text: Before play: what would make this hotfix safe to ship tonight?
question.why: A name, a person's word and a local test are all claims. Provenance from the pipeline is evidence.

options.label: It has the right name and version number
You can show where it was built, and from what
A senior engineer says it is fine
It worked on the author's machine
